topic.title: Moving back costs the second offer
topic.claim: Moving back to a tier-2 city saves you rent but quietly costs you something nobody counts: your next job offer.
topic.moment: You work remotely from your hometown, life is cheaper, and the recruiter calls stop.

turn.believed: Moving back is just a cost-of-living win.
turn.actually: Big cities pay you for the options you have, not just the job you hold.

topic.feeling: Happier at home, and slowly afraid I've fallen off the map.
topic.villain: Job markets packed into a few metros
topic.because: Your salary rises when another company wants you. Fewer companies around you means fewer reasons for anyone to pay you more.
topic.payoff: Before you move, count how many companies within an hour of you would hire you tomorrow. That's what you're giving up.
topic.behaviour: Professionals move home for remote roles and see their salary growth slow down.
topic.mechanism: Pay grows with competing offers, and offers live in metros.
topic.group: Remote and hybrid professionals weighing a move home
topic.send_to: The friend who keeps saying 'I'll just work from home in my city'.
topic.why_now: Remote roles are shrinking while metro rents keep rising, and a lot of people are doing this maths right now.

score.why: Going home looks like a cost win, but you give up the job options that push your salary up; mixed feelings, a real turn.
